description: Reads from the local LevelDB cache, which may lag behind Copilot's server if the macOS app hasn't synced recently. For real-time data use --live-reads with `get_transactions_live`. Unified transaction retrieval tool. Supports multiple modes: (1) Filter-based: Use period, date range, category, merchant, amount filters. (2) Single lookup: Provide transaction_id to get one transaction. (3) Text search: Use query for free-text merchant search. (4) Special types: Use transaction_type for foreign, refunds, credits, duplicates, hsa_eligible, tagged. (5) Location-based: Use city or lat/lon with radius_km. (6) Tag filter: Use tag to find transactions with a specific tag. Rows are TERSE by default: transaction_id, date, amount, name, category_name, account_id, item_id, pending, excluded, internal_transfer. `excluded` answers "is this row excluded from spending?" — the raw per-transaction flag OR the row's category being user-excluded, the same union exclude_excluded filters on — so it is true for a row Copilot never stamped individually. It is therefore nearly always false in a default response, since exclude_excluded already removed those rows; it carries information only when you pass exclude_excluded: false. A cache row carries ~30 fields and most callers need a handful, so the rest are excluded unless asked for. PARTIAL list of what that drops, not exhaustive: Plaid metadata (plaid_category_id, plaid_category_strings, plaid_deleted), internal IDs (category_id, recurring_id, goal_id, parent_transaction_id, children_transaction_ids, user_id), enrichment and intelligence fields (normalized_merchant — still the normalized merchant name when requested — intelligence_suggested_category_ids, suggestion_ids, original_name), tag_ids, review state (user_reviewed, user_note, user_changed_type — true only when a human re-typed the row, so do not second-guess its type), location (city, region, country, lat/lon), and flags like is_amazon/from_investment. `amazon` is worth naming because nothing else hints it exists: on rows Copilot matched to an Amazon order it carries the receipt — {order_id, items: [{id, name, link, price, quantity}], other: {giftWrapping, rewards, savings, shipping, tax}} — so fields: ["default", "amazon"] answers "what was in this order" without an exported CSV. Ask for any of them by name with fields: ["default", "tag_ids"], or take the whole document with fields: ["all"] (or "*"). category_name is always resolved to a human-readable name. `compact` was removed in v3.0.0 — passing it now raises an error naming this migration.

category.description: Filter by category ID from get_categories (exact match, not a name). A parent category's id also returns its subcategories' rows. An id that belongs to no category and to no transaction the call looked at is an error.

country.description: Filter by country code (e.g., US, CL)

exclude_deleted.description: Exclude deleted transactions marked by Plaid (default: true)

exclude_split_parents.description: Exclude split-transaction parents (docs with children_transaction_ids). The children already carry the real categorized amounts — returning the parent would double-count the spend. Default: true.

exclude_transfers.description: Exclude transfers between accounts and credit card payments (default: true)

fields.description: Return only these fields per transaction. Default when omitted: a terse row (transaction_id, date, amount, name, category_name, account_id, item_id, pending, excluded, internal_transfer). Anything else is requestable by name alongside the preset: fields: ["default", "tag_ids"], or "all" / "*" for the whole row. THIS TOOL's own description names what its rows drop — the two modes drop different things, because a live row is not a cache document. The note is user_note in cache mode and user_notes live; either spelling works in either mode, and each mode returns its own. Unknown names are omitted and reported via _field_warning.

lat.description: Latitude for proximity search (use with lon and radius_km)

lon.description: Longitude for proximity search (use with lat and radius_km)

offset.description: Number of results to skip for pagination (default: 0)

pending.description: Filter by pending status (true for pending only, false for settled only)

period.description: Period shorthand: this_month, last_month, last_7_days, last_30_days, last_90_days, ytd, this_year, last_year

transaction_id.description: Get a single transaction by ID (ignores other filters, though a `category` value must still be a real id)

transaction_type.description: Filter by special type. Cache-only: foreign (international) and duplicates (potential duplicate transactions, paired among the rows the other filters keep; pass the matching exclude_*: false, e.g. exclude_deleted: false, to bring a hidden copy back). Same rule in cache and live mode (positive amount = money out). refunds: a negative REGULAR row in a spending category; never INCOME, a transfer or uncategorized. credits: a negative REGULAR row whose name has credit/cashback/reward/rebate/bonus and whose category is not income or transfer; may overlap refunds. hsa_eligible: a heuristic, not an eligibility ruling: a positive REGULAR row whose category name has health/medical/pharmac/dental/eye care/vision or whose name has cvs/walgreens/pharmacy/medical/dental/vision/hospital. tagged: has a tag. type_specific_data totals cover all matching rows, not just the returned page.

name: get_transactions
